content.user_title: Build Azure Service Bus Messaging in Python
content.value_statement: Azure Service Bus projects need clear patterns for queues, topics, sessions, and dead-letter flows. This skill provides focused Python SDK guidance for reliable enterprise messaging.
actual_capabilities: Shows package installation for azure-servicebus and azure-identity.
Demonstrates async sending and receiving for queues.
Covers receive modes, settlement actions, and dead-letter handling.
Summarizes topics, subscriptions, sessions, and scheduled messages.
limitations: Does not provision Azure resources or manage access policies.
Examples use placeholders that must be replaced for each environment.
Requires installed Azure SDK packages and valid Azure credentials.
Referenced helper scripts and reference pages are not included in the scanned package.

use_cases.title: Create Queue Workers
use_cases.description: Build Python producers and consumers that send, receive, complete, abandon, or dead-letter queue messages.

use_cases.title: Standardize Messaging Patterns
use_cases.description: Use consistent guidance for topics, subscriptions, sessions, scheduled messages, and receive modes across services.

use_cases.title: Improve Failure Handling
use_cases.description: Plan dead-letter queue review, poison message handling, and settlement choices for unreliable processing paths.

prompt_templates.title: Set Up a Client
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me configure a Python Azure Service Bus client using DefaultAzureCredential. Include the required environment values and setup steps.

prompt_templates.title: Build Queue Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a plan for an async Python queue producer and consumer. Include batching, receive wait time, and message completion.

prompt_templates.title: Design Topic Consumers
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design a Python publisher and subscription consumer for an Azure Service Bus topic. Explain receiving and settlement decisions.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Resilient Processing
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Service Bus processing design for sessions, scheduled messages, and dead-letter handling. Identify reliability gaps and safer settlement choices.

output_examples.input: I need a Python worker that receives queue messages reliably.
output_examples.output: A concise implementation outline with authentication choices, receive mode guidance, settlement rules, and retry considerations.

output_examples.input: My topic subscribers need ordered processing for related events.
output_examples.output: A sessions-focused design summary that explains message grouping, receiver selection, and completion behavior.

output_examples.input: Messages are moving to the dead-letter queue.
output_examples.output: A troubleshooting checklist covering failure reasons, review steps, reprocessing options, and safer handling rules.

best_practices: Use async clients for production workloads that handle many messages.
Use context managers so clients, senders, and receivers close cleanly.
Complete, abandon, defer, or dead-letter each message based on processing results.
anti_patterns: Do not use placeholder namespaces, queue names, or credentials in real environments.
Do not receive and delete messages when reliable processing is required.
Do not ignore dead-letter queues after repeated processing failures.

faq.question: Can this skill create Azure Service Bus resources?
faq.answer: No. It explains Python SDK usage and references resource names, but resource provisioning is outside the included file.

faq.question: Does it support asynchronous Python code?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance includes async client patterns for sending, receiving, batching, and settling messages.

faq.question: Which authentication method does it show?
faq.answer: It shows DefaultAzureCredential with ServiceBusClient for Azure identity based authentication.

faq.question: Can it help with dead-letter queues?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains receiving from the dead-letter subqueue and completing reviewed dead-letter messages.

faq.question: Does it include production-ready helper scripts?
faq.answer: No. The scanned package contains SKILL.md only, so validate generated code and operational steps before use.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: Claude, Codex, and Claude Code can use the Markdown guidance in this skill.
